subject: Presubmission inquiry & collaboration — evidence standards for physical-risk disclosure regimes
body:
Dear Editors,

I am preparing a policy analysis for Climate Policy: "Disclosure regimes without evidence standards: provenance classes for EU Taxonomy, CSRD and Pillar 3 physical-risk reporting".

The article analyses a gap across the EU's disclosure architecture: the EU Taxonomy's DNSH climate-adaptation test, CSRD/ESRS E1 and EBA Pillar 3 ESG all require assessments of material physical climate risks, but none defines a standard for the provenance of the underlying evidence. We propose an operational provenance classification (observed / documented / reported / modelled / inferred / unknown), show how it maps onto the existing regulatory texts, and discuss implications for supervisors, verifiers and future standard-setting.

Would this be of interest to the journal, and which submission category would you suggest? Beyond this article, we would welcome collaboration with the Climate Policy community — for example contributing practitioner evidence from disclosure-support work, or participating in special issues on climate-risk disclosure and finance policy.

Kind regards,
Motaz OMARIEN. Talaix
Earth Observation & Environmental Risk
Financial Decision Intelligence
Luxembourg-based technology team
